questions.q: What is AWS Bedrock, at its core?
options: AWS's managed service for calling foundation models from multiple providers through one API
A GPU VM family inside AWS, similar to Azure's NC-series
A code editor built specifically for training AI models
A service that only hosts Amazon's own models, with no third-party providers
questions.explain: Bedrock is AWS's managed service for accessing foundation models from Amazon and multiple third-party providers through one unified API.

questions.q: What does Bedrock's model picker actually let you choose between?
options: Only different AWS regions to deploy the same model to
Models from multiple providers — Amazon, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral AI, Cohere, and others — grouped in one console
Only Amazon's own Titan models, with no other vendors
Different pricing tiers for the exact same single model
questions.explain: Bedrock groups multiple model providers in one console and API, rather than requiring a separate account per vendor.

questions.q: What does the Test Agent window let you verify before an agent goes to production?
options: The agent's monthly AWS bill
Whether the agent's underlying VM has enough disk space
How a conversation unfolds turn by turn, including reviewing a tool call's output before submitting it to let the agent continue
Which AWS region has the cheapest pricing for that model
questions.explain: The Test Agent panel steps through a conversation, pausing on tool calls so you can review output before approving it to continue.

questions.q: What does Bedrock's Converse API actually standardize?
options: It standardizes billing across all AWS services, not just Bedrock
It requires a completely different request format for each model provider
The same request/response shape across every model provider Bedrock hosts
It only works with Anthropic's Claude models
questions.explain: The Converse API gives one unified call shape regardless of which provider's model is behind model-id — Claude, Titan, or others.

questions.q: What does 'IAM-native' mean as a reason teams choose Bedrock?
options: Bedrock requires a completely separate login system from the rest of AWS
Bedrock access uses the exact same AWS identity and permission model as the rest of an AWS account
IAM stands for 'Inference And Model' pricing
It means Bedrock can only be used by AWS's internal teams
questions.explain: Bedrock plugs into the same IAM identity and permission system already used across an AWS account, rather than a separate auth layer.
